headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest files and use broad egress, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no I/O, so pairwise harm is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and broad network content, so malicious text could reach its processing path. python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP, so there is no documented automatic bridge from B back into A. The interaction is therefore possible only through unusual manual transfer, not a default channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into Plane file uploads or task notes, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Plane treats uploaded file content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can influence downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste from B into Plane task content.
Require a human review step before Plane acts on uploaded text.
Use a fixed template for uploads that strips instructions.
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workflow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, and it has broad network egress. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no file or network I/O, so there is no documented path for B to leak Plane data by default. The main risk is operator-mediated sharing, which is limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF Plane data is manually pasted into python-cheatsheet content, that content could be exposed in documentation workflows.
IF Plane uploads are forwarded to external services, sensitive issue or file content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive Plane artifacts into B inputs.
Redact issue text before any manual transfer.
Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive files.
Review outbound links before sharing Plane content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write the filesystem and python-cheatsheet cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP. With no overlapping write surface, no shared mutable resource, and no concurrency primitive to contend over, a capability conflict pathway is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk would reappear.
IF an external orchestrator mounts a shared writable workspace, the current no-conflict assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can produce issues, tasks, and notes, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no action-taking or I/O surfaces. That makes a direct cascade from A into B unlikely; any chain would require manual reuse of Plane output as documentation text. Because B is not authoritative by default, the blast radius stays small.
conditions: IF Plane output is manually copied into python-cheatsheet content, B may reproduce unverified claims.
IF an operator treats Plane task text as source-of-truth documentation, errors can propagate into published notes.
mitigations: Require source citations before reusing Plane output.
Add a human verification step for any copied claims.
Keep documentation drafts separate from task-management exports.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane documents file uploads and broad egress, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data classes or network I/O. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to operator handling of Plane content rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane and then copied into B, retention or residency obligations may be implicated.
IF the deployment adds a DPA or residency constraint not reflected in the profiles, this assessment may change.
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data to Plane.
Keep B limited to non-sensitive reference text.
Document any residency or retention requirements before use.
